messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p95 latency increase on runtime-prod-eu (service: inference-runtime) — spike detected at 12:03 UTC. Kernel-fallback rate rising, batching success rate down 35%. Auto-canary: v2.5.1 -> v2.6.0 rolled 3m ago. Paging: escalated. @oncall-ryan paging now.

deploy-bot: Deploy v2.6.0 to runtime-prod finished at 12:00:12 UTC. Canary 5% traffic. No immediate errors reported from CI smoke.

oncall-ryan: @here I’m on it. seeing p50 up ~40ms, p95 +800ms on EU region. Kernel fallback % per GPU at 22% (baseline 0.7%). Queues backing up on batcher pods.

maya: Any customer-facing 5xxs?

oncall-ryan: No hard 5xxs in the first minute but tail latency causing timeouts at app layer — our retries are bubbling. A couple of customer sessions hit 504 from the gateway.

sre-lina: I’m pulling the runbooks. Paging the runtime team. Metrics I care about: kernel_fallback_rate, batch_success_rate, kv_cache_hit, in_flight_requests.

eng-runtime-tom: saw trace samples: fallback happens during long-seq attention kernel selection. Looks like kernel chooser picks a slower fallback path under new binary. Possibly a codepath regression for fused attention when sequence len > 1024.

product-elsa: Which customers saw timeouts? any large tenants?

oncall-ryan: Early logs show increased latency for a small set of heavy-enterprise customers on EU-west-2. Two VIP customers reported degraded throughput (reducing effective qps by ~30% for them).

customer-jones: Our team saw request times jump from ~120ms to 900ms, intermittent 504s for chat endpoints. We opened a ticket. We're throttling client-side for now.

ops-nina: Getting a timeline together. If canary is bad, we should kill the canary traffic or flip kill-flag, not a full rollback yet. Need to confirm if fix is in next patch.

eng-runtime-tom: Agreed. Kill-flag available: feature.flag.runtime.v2_6_kernelsafe -> default true. Flipping to false will route to previous kernel selection; should reduce fallback.

oncall-ryan: Can we flip the flag safely for canary-only?

deploy-bot: flag flip request queued. Command: `redwoodctl flags set feature.flag.runtime.v2_6_kernelsafe false --scope canary`

oncall-ryan: Running it now.

oncall-ryan: (runs) `redwoodctl flags set feature.flag.runtime.v2_6_kernelsafe false --scope canary`

deploy-bot: Flag flipped for canary. Confirmed: 5% of traffic now on fallback-safe kernel path.

sre-lina: Metrics 90s after flip: kernel_fallback_rate in canary down to 3%. batch_success_rate improving +12%. Latency trending down but tail still high, probably queued requests draining.

maya: Any customer impact improvement?

customer-jones: We still see some 504s but tail latency has reduced for our traffic. Thanks.

eng-runtime-tom: Looks promising but not resolved for all nodes — some GPUs are still thrashing into fallback due to prefetch/batcher ordering. My hunch: new runtime changed batch packing heuristics, causing longer batches for certain seq distributions leading to memory pressure and kernel fallback.

oncall-ryan: Two mitigation options: 1) keep kill-flag on and monitor (let canary finish with modified behavior), 2) rapid rollback of v2.6.0 canary to v2.5.1 to stop further risk. Thoughts?

product-elsa: We should prioritize stability for enterprise customers. If kill-flag quickfix shows steady metrics for next 10-15m, prefer that to avoid cache/thaw issues. But be ready to rollback if noisy.

eng-runtime-tom: Give me 10m to validate kernel selection logs across all canary hosts. If we still see >5% fallback on more than 1 node, we should rollback the canary.

sre-lina: notifying support and preparing customer-impact note. Drafting now: "We are investigating intermittent timeouts and elevated inference latency in EU region after a partial release. Impact: a small subset of enterprise customers experiencing degraded latency and occasional gateway timeouts. Engineers are on mitigation."

ops-nina: If rollback: command `redwoodctl rollout cancel --release v2.6.0 --target canary` then `redwoodctl deploy --release v2.5.1 --target canary` (we have automated rollback job). Also need to coordinate session preservation for sticky sessions — `--preserve-sessions` flag available.

oncall-ryan: 10m check. Metrics continue to improve: p95 down ~40% vs peak, kernel_fallback for canary median 2.6%, queue length decreasing.

eng-runtime-tom: Confirming across canary nodes: 4/5 are good, one node still shows fallback spikes tied to batcher reordering. I suspect a config drift on that host (older kernel mapping).

oncall-ryan: Can we isolate that host from rotation?

deploy-bot: Draining node: `kubectl cordon node/canary-eu-7 && kubectl drain node/canary-eu-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

eng-runtime-tom: Drained. New requests routing away. That node had leftover kernel cache from previous deploy step — rewarm path is broken.

sre-lina: Great. After drain, kernel fallback cluster-wide now ~1.8%, p95 returning to baseline. No new 504 reports in last 8m.

customer-jones: Confirming: our 99th is back to normal. Thanks for the quick response.

maya: Should we keep canary running with kill-flag off? handle config drift?

eng-runtime-tom: I want to keep kill-flag off (i.e., the safe path enabled) for canary until we push a patched v2.6.1 that has kernel chooser fix and batcher config guardrail. Also will add a predeploy check to validate kernel cache warming.

product-elsa: Timeline for patch?

eng-runtime-tom: I can have a patch built & unit-tested in 1.5h, canary ready in ~2h. If metrics stay stable we can roll the patch through canary then staged rollout.

ops-nina: Ops note: because we drained one canary node, we might briefly under-provision canary capacity — watch error budget for those customers.

oncall-ryan: Support and I will notify the impacted customers with interim RCA: short-term cause - new kernel selection + batch packing change causing kernel fallback and queueing on certain sequence-length distributions. Mitigation - flipped canary-safe kernel flag and drained misbehaving host; rollback not required. Next steps - replace canary host, patch runtime, add predeploy checks.

sre-lina: Posting incident severity: Sev 2 (degraded performance for small % of customers, active mitigation, no data loss).

product-elsa: Please include a blameless postmortem timeline in the follow-up and add a note to the release playbook about session-preserve flags.

eng-runtime-tom: Filed issue: RUNTIME-8472 "kernel chooser regression w/ batch packing" — linked to PR for v2.6.1.

customer-jones: Appreciate the transparency — keep us posted on the patch ETA.

noncall-ryan: Will follow up when patch is live. For now, leaving the canary running with feature.flag.runtime.v2_6_kernelsafe=false and draining any node that shows cache miswarm.

sre-lina: Handing off to oncall-ryan for post-incident tracking. @oncall-ryan please add to the incident tracker with notes and assignees for RUNTIME-8472.

oncall-ryan: Done. Incident tracker updated, assignees: tom (runtime), lina (sre), nina (ops), maya (customer comms). I’ll stay on until patch rolled.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=2, status=mitigated (partial), pages=sent, linked_issue=RUNTIME-8472, runbook=runtime-kernel-fallback.md

eng-runtime-tom: Quick log snippet for posterity: ```
GRPC call id=0x9af3 seq_len=1536 kernel_choice=fallback mem_err=None batch_size=32 -> slow kernel selected
GRPC call id=0x9b12 seq_len=512 kernel_choice=optimized mem_err=None batch_size=16 -> ok
```

ops-nina: I'll schedule a brief handoff post-mortem at 14:30 UTC to confirm rollout steps and predeploy checks.

product-elsa: Thanks everyone. Keeping affected customers informed.

customer-jones: Thanks, team.

oncall-ryan: closing thread for now; will re-open if rollback becomes necessary.
